comparison: Both strongly support the computational methodology (C4, C38, C95-C104). OpenEval emphasizes statistical validation and parameter robustness, while peer reviewers praised methods as 'solid' and 'particularly compelling,' noting authors addressed GNM limitations. High agreement on methodological validity.

Both support computational predictions with strong statistical validation (C39-C41). OpenEval highlights p=9×e⁻¹³ significance and NBD2 asymmetry alignment with experiments. Peer reviewers found TE analysis 'particularly compelling' and praised identification of key allosteric residues. Strong concordance.

Both address pre-existing dynamic infrastructure in ATP-free state (C45-C47). OpenEval considers this a reasonable computational inference, while peer reviewers accepted ATP-free dynamics findings as 'generally solid' without challenge. Agreement on ATP-free state characterization.

Both address NBD2 asymmetry (C42-C44). OpenEval notes alignment with single-molecule studies, while peer reviewers accepted asymmetry findings as part of the broader allosteric mechanism without objection. Concordant support.

Both address mode-removal analysis and allosteric site identification (C48-C50). OpenEval validates ivacaftor site from structural studies and accepts TMD1 cluster as novel prediction. Peer reviewers accepted the novel allosteric hotspot discovery as 'significant for understanding CFTR biology.' Agreement on findings.

Both support ATP-induced changes in dynamics (C51-C56). OpenEval describes focusing of dynamics and entropy shifts directly observed in computational data. Peer reviewers accepted ATP-dependent transitions as part of 'comprehensive discussion of proposed mechanism.' Strong concordance.

Both address hierarchical mode analysis (C57-C58). OpenEval supports mode-removal findings as internally consistent. Peer reviewers accepted hierarchical mode analysis without criticism, noting 'comprehensive insights into allosteric mechanism.' Agreement on approach.

Both address novel allosteric hotspot (C10, C59-C60). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative druggability claim (C94) requiring experimental validation. Peer reviewers SUPPORTED the discovery without challenge, accepting therapeutic implications. Divergence: OpenEval more cautious about druggability speculation.

Both address druggability claim (C94). OpenEval considers this speculative and requiring experimental validation (UNCERTAIN rating). Peer reviewers accepted therapeutic implications without objection (SUPPORTED). Clear disagreement on confidence level for druggability claims.

Both support asymmetric NBD connectivity findings (C63-C64). OpenEval notes direct computational observation with experimental citation support. Peer reviewers accepted asymmetry as part of disease mutation characterization. Strong agreement.

Both address ANM-LD simulation results (C61-C62, C65). OpenEval supports rigid body motion interpretation from cross-correlation patterns. Peer reviewers accepted ANM-LD trajectory and conformational pathway as 'validated with experimental observations.' Concordant support.

Both support temporal allosteric signaling pathway (C66-C69). OpenEval validates time-delayed correlation methodology and pathway alignment with Levring et al. 2023. Peer reviewers accepted signal propagation pathway as part of 'comprehensive discussion of proposed mechanism.' Strong agreement.

Both strongly support drug mechanism analysis (C74-C79). OpenEval highlights quantitative correlation (r=0.83) between ivacaftor and ATP signaling. Peer reviewers accepted drug mechanism insights without challenge as 'significant for understanding CFTR biology.' High concordance.

Both address hybrid allosteric mechanism (C82, C88). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to significant speculation and lack of direct experimental validation of ensemble selection component. Peer reviewers SUPPORTED the proposed mechanism, explicitly appreciating 'comprehensive discussion.' Divergence: OpenEval more cautious about speculative mechanistic model.

Both address experimental evidence for allosteric mechanism (C80-C86). OpenEval acknowledges cited experimental support but considers integrated mechanism speculative (UNCERTAIN). Peer reviewers accepted background framework and experimental context without challenge (SUPPORTED). Difference in confidence about mechanistic integration.

Both support dynamic mechanism for channel opening (C93). OpenEval notes convergent experimental evidence though representing inference rather than direct observation. Peer reviewers appreciated comprehensive mechanistic discussion. Agreement on dynamic mechanism.

Both address evidence that channel opening doesn't require major conformational changes (C89-C92). OpenEval supports synthesis from multiple cited studies. Peer reviewers accepted background information and experimental observations. Concordant support.

Both address disease mutation correlation (C6). OpenEval notes statistical significance from Figure 1-supplement 6. Peer reviewers praised identification of 'key residues that may account for disease mutations.' Strong agreement on this finding.

Both address pre-existing dynamics claim (C7). OpenEval supports this from computational analysis comparing ATP states. Peer reviewers accepted ATP-free dynamics characterization as part of overall mechanism. Agreement on pre-existing dynamics.
Both address ATP-induced focusing of dynamics (C8). OpenEval supports from comparative state analysis. Peer reviewers accepted ATP-dependent transitions. Concordant support.
Both address drug mechanism summary (C9). OpenEval supports based on quantitative correlation analysis. Peer reviewers accepted drug mechanism insights. Agreement on this key finding.

Both support background on CF and CFTR (C1-C27). OpenEval confirms accurate representation of established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accepted background information and context, appreciating comprehensive discussion. Strong concordance on foundational claims.

Both support background on allosteric models and CFTR allostery (C28-C37). OpenEval validates accurate descriptions of KNF, MWC, and dynamic mechanisms with proper citations. Peer reviewers accepted background framework for protein allostery. Agreement on theoretical context.

Both support background on FDA-approved CF drugs (C70-C73). OpenEval confirms well-established therapeutic information with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers accepted background without challenge. Concordant support for established drug information.
